title: Mocks
description:
You can create a mock function or a class to track its execution with the vi.fn method. If you want to track a property on an already created object, you can use the vi.spyOn method:

You should use mock assertions (e.g., toHaveBeenCalled) on expect to assert mock results. This API reference describes available properties and methods to manipulate mock behavior.

entries.name: Mocks
entries.description:
You can create a mock function or a class to track its execution with the vi.fn method. If you want to track a property on an already created object, you can use the vi.spyOn method:

You should use mock assertions (e.g., toHaveBeenCalled) on expect to assert mock results. This API reference describes available properties and methods to manipulate mock behavior.

examples.code:
mock.mockReturnValue({ hello: () => 'world' }) 
mock.mockImplementation(class { hello = () => 'world' })

notes: TIPThe custom function implementation in the types below is marked with a generic <T>.

children.name: getMockImplementation
children.description:
Returns the current mock implementation if there is one. If an implementation was queued with mockImplementationOnce, it returns the first queued implementation instead.

If the mock was created with vi.fn, it will use the provided method as the mock implementation.

If the mock was created with vi.spyOn, it will return undefined unless a custom implementation is provided.

examples.code: function getMockImplementation(): T | undefined

children.name: getMockName
children.description: Use it to return the name assigned to the mock with the .mockName(name) method. By default, vi.fn() mocks will return 'vi.fn()', while spies created with vi.spyOn will keep the original name.

examples.code: function getMockName(): string

children.name: mockClear
children.description:
Clears all information about every call. After calling it, all properties on .mock will return to their initial state. This method does not reset implementations. It is useful for cleaning up mocks between different assertions.

To automatically call this method before each test, enable the clearMocks setting in the configuration.

examples.code: function mockClear(): Mock<T>

children.name: mockName
children.description: Sets the internal mock name. This is useful for identifying the mock when an assertion fails.

examples.code: function mockName(name: string): Mock<T>

children.name: mockImplementation
children.description:
Accepts a function to be used as the mock implementation. TypeScript expects the arguments and return type to match those of the original function.

If the implementation is a class, the mock's prototype is re-pointed to the implementation's prototype, so constructed instances see its prototype methods and pass instanceof checks against it. See Mocking Classes for details.

examples.code: function mockImplementation(fn: T): Mock<T>

children.name: mockImplementationOnce
children.description:
Accepts a function to be used as the mock implementation. TypeScript expects the arguments and return type to match those of the original function. This method can be chained to produce different results for multiple function calls.

When the mocked function runs out of implementations, it will invoke the default implementation set with vi.fn(() => defaultValue) or .mockImplementation(() => defaultValue) if they were called:

examples.code: function mockImplementationOnce(fn: T): Mock<T>

const myMockFn = vi
  .fn()
  .mockImplementationOnce(() => true) // 1st call
  .mockImplementationOnce(() => false) // 2nd call

myMockFn() // 1st call: true
myMockFn() // 2nd call: false

const myMockFn = vi
  .fn(() => 'default')
  .mockImplementationOnce(() => 'first call')
  .mockImplementationOnce(() => 'second call')

// 'first call', 'second call', 'default', 'default'
console.log(myMockFn(), myMockFn(), myMockFn(), myMockFn())

children.name: withImplementation
children.description:
Overrides the original mock implementation temporarily while the callback is being executed.

Can be used with an asynchronous callback. The method has to be awaited to use the original implementation afterward.

Note that this method takes precedence over the mockImplementationOnce.

children.name: mockRejectedValue
children.description: Accepts an error that will be rejected when an async function is called.

examples.code: function mockRejectedValue(value: unknown): Mock<T>

const asyncMock = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('Async error'))

await asyncMock() // throws Error<'Async error'>

children.name: mockRejectedValueOnce
children.description: Accepts a value that will be rejected during the next function call. If chained, each consecutive call will reject the specified value.

examples.code: function mockRejectedValueOnce(value: unknown): Mock<T>

const asyncMock = vi
  .fn()
  .mockResolvedValueOnce('first call')
  .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('Async error'))

await asyncMock() // 'first call'
await asyncMock() // throws Error<'Async error'>

children.name: mockReset
children.description:
Does what mockClear does and resets the mock implementation. This also resets all "once" implementations.

Note that resetting a mock from vi.fn() will set the implementation to an empty function that returns undefined. Resetting a mock from vi.fn(impl) will reset the implementation to impl.

The mock's prototype chain follows along: it reverts to the original class for vi.fn(impl) and vi.spyOn(), and to a plain object for vi.fn(), so instances constructed after the reset no longer pass instanceof checks against a previously set class implementation.

This is useful when you want to reset a mock to its original state.

To automatically call this method before each test, enable the mockReset setting in the configuration.

examples.code: function mockReset(): Mock<T>

children.name: mockRestore
children.description:
Does what mockReset does and restores the original descriptors of spied-on objects, if the mock was created with vi.spyOn.

mockRestore on a vi.fn() mock is identical to mockReset.

To automatically call this method before each test, enable the restoreMocks setting in the configuration.

examples.code: function mockRestore(): void

children.name: mockResolvedValue
children.description: Accepts a value that will be resolved when the async function is called. TypeScript will only accept values that match the return type of the original function.

examples.code: function mockResolvedValue(value: Awaited<ReturnType<T>>): Mock<T>

const asyncMock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(42)

await asyncMock() // 42

children.name: mockResolvedValueOnce
children.description: Accepts a value that will be resolved during the next function call. TypeScript will only accept values that match the return type of the original function. If chained, each consecutive call will resolve the specified value.

examples.code: function mockResolvedValueOnce(value: Awaited<ReturnType<T>>): Mock<T>

const asyncMock = vi
  .fn()
  .mockResolvedValue('default')
  .mockResolvedValueOnce('first call')
  .mockResolvedValueOnce('second call')

await asyncMock() // first call
await asyncMock() // second call
await asyncMock() // default
await asyncMock() // default

children.name: mockReturnThis
children.description: Use this if you need to return the this context from the method without invoking the actual implementation. This is a shorthand for:

examples.code: function mockReturnThis(): Mock<T>

children.name: mockReturnValue
children.description: Accepts a value that will be returned whenever the mock function is called. TypeScript will only accept values that match the return type of the original function.

examples.code: function mockReturnValue(value: ReturnType<T>): Mock<T>

const mock = vi.fn()
mock.mockReturnValue(42)
mock() // 42
mock.mockReturnValue(43)
mock() // 43

children.name: mockReturnValueOnce
children.description:
Accepts a value that will be returned during the next function call. TypeScript will only accept values that match the return type of the original function. If chained, each consecutive call will return the specified value.

When the mocked function runs out of implementations, it will invoke the default implementation set with vi.fn(() => defaultValue) or .mockImplementation(() => defaultValue) if they were called:

examples.code: function mockReturnValueOnce(value: ReturnType<T>): Mock<T>

const myMockFn = vi
  .fn()
  .mockReturnValue('default')
  .mockReturnValueOnce('first call')
  .mockReturnValueOnce('second call')

// 'first call', 'second call', 'default', 'default'
console.log(myMockFn(), myMockFn(), myMockFn(), myMockFn())

children.name: mockThrow 4.1.0+
children.description: Accepts a value that will be thrown whenever the mock function is called.

examples.code: function mockThrow(value: unknown): Mock<T>

children.name: mockThrowOnce 4.1.0+
children.description: Accepts a value that will be thrown during the next function call. If chained, every consecutive call will throw the specified value.

examples.code: function mockThrowOnce(value: unknown): Mock<T>

const myMockFn = vi
  .fn()
  .mockReturnValue('default')
  .mockThrowOnce(new Error('first call error'))
  .mockThrowOnce('second call error')

expect(() => myMockFn()).toThrow('first call error')
expect(() => myMockFn()).toThrow('second call error')
expect(myMockFn()).toEqual('default')

children.name: mock.calls
children.description: This is an array containing all arguments for each call. One item of the array is the arguments of that call.

examples.code: const calls: Parameters<T>[]

children.name: mock.lastCall
children.description: This contains the arguments of the last call. If the mock wasn't called, it will return undefined.

examples.code: const lastCall: Parameters<T> | undefined

children.name: mock.results
children.description:
This is an array containing all values that were returned from the function. One item of the array is an object with properties type and value. Available types are:

The value property contains the returned value or thrown error. If the function returned a Promise, then result will always be 'return' even if the promise was rejected.
notes: 'incomplete' - the function did not finish running yet.

children.name: mock.settledResults
children.description:
An array containing all values that were resolved or rejected by the function.

If the function returned non-promise values, the value will be kept as is, but the type will still say fulfilled or rejected.

Until the value is resolved or rejected, the settledResult type will be incomplete.

children.name: mock.invocationCallOrder
children.description: This property returns the order of the mock function's execution. It is an array of numbers that are shared between all defined mocks.

examples.code: const invocationCallOrder: number[]

const fn1 = vi.fn()
const fn2 = vi.fn()

fn1()
fn2()
fn1()

fn1.mock.invocationCallOrder === [1, 3]
fn2.mock.invocationCallOrder === [2]

children.name: mock.contexts
children.description: This property is an array of this values used during each call to the mock function. If the mock was called with the new keyword, the value is the same as in mock.instances.
signatures:
type MockProcedureContext<T> = T extends new (...args: any[]) => any
  ? InstanceType<T>
  : ThisParameterType<T>

const contexts: MockProcedureContext<T>[]

examples.code:
type MockProcedureContext<T> = T extends new (...args: any[]) => any
  ? InstanceType<T>
  : ThisParameterType<T>

const contexts: MockProcedureContext<T>[]

children.name: mock.instances
children.description:
This property is an array with one value for each call to the mock function. If the mock was called with the new keyword, the value is the object that new returned, or undefined if the constructor threw an error. Otherwise, the value is the context (this) of the call, the same as in mock.contexts.

If the implementation returns an object from the constructor, mock.instances stores that object:

examples.code: const instances: MockProcedureContext<T>[]
